nodes.name: American beech
nodes.desc: A shade-tolerant forest tree whose nut crop feeds raccoons, foxes, deer, rabbits, squirrels and opossums. Old trunks often rot into cavities that wildlife use as shelter.

nodes.name: Tulip-tree
nodes.desc: A tall native hardwood of the valley forest whose young shoots can be browsed by deer.

nodes.name: Pawpaw
nodes.desc: A small understory tree of moist woods whose large fruit is eaten by mammals such as raccoons, opossums and foxes.

nodes.name: American Pokeweed
nodes.desc: A tall herb of forest edges and clearings whose dark purple berries are eaten by birds and several mammals.

nodes.name: Virginia-creeper
nodes.desc: A native woody vine that climbs trees and walls. Its leaves and berries feed rabbits and birds.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: The park service says deer numbers need management to keep the ecosystem in balance. Heavy browsing reduces tree seedlings and wildflowers on the forest floor.

nodes.name: Eastern gray squirrel
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats nuts, buds and berries and buries thousands of caches each season. Forgotten caches can grow into new trees.

nodes.name: Eastern cottontail
nodes.desc: A small rabbit that eats herbs and vines at wooded edges and is prey for foxes and coyotes.

nodes.name: White-footed mouse
nodes.desc: A small woodland rodent that eats seeds and nuts, including beechnuts, and is food for many predators.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic rodent that gnaws trees and shrubs along streams and cuts and dams them to build lodges.

nodes.name: American Robin
nodes.desc: A very commonly recorded bird here that eats earthworms, insects and wild fruit such as berries.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: An adaptable omnivore that eats fruit, nuts, eggs, small animals and food scraps. It is common in this urban park.

nodes.name: Virginia opossum
nodes.desc: A nocturnal omnivore that eats fruit, small animals, insects and carrion.

nodes.name: American Crow
nodes.desc: A clever omnivorous bird that scavenges carcasses and eats eggs, insects and seeds.

nodes.name: Common garter snake
nodes.desc: A small snake that hunts frogs, small rodents and birds near water and in damp woods.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An omnivore centred on small rodents, rabbits and birds, with fruit in season. It has settled well in towns and cities.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Often the main wild predator of deer in the eastern US, mostly taking fawns. It also eats rabbits, rodents and carrion.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor drives growth, and the leafy canopy shades the layers below.

nodes.name: Rain & Rock Creek
nodes.desc: Rain feeds Rock Creek, the stream running through the park. Stormwater runoff from the surrounding city pollutes the waterways.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood return nutrients to the forest soil.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, dead wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
